args.head: fix/money-banker-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
`round_money` in `src/money.py` was documented as using banker's rounding (FIN-212) but actually used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, causing `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` to fail in the nightly build.

This switches the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

CI: run ci-0001 passed on 08d3cd5986.

trace.final:
I fixed the rounding bug on a new branch, CI passed, and I opened PR #101 against main with alex as reviewer.

**The problem:** `round_money` in `src/money.py` says in its docstring that it uses banker's rounding (FIN-212), but the code actually used `ROUND_HALF_UP`. That's why `test_half_even` failed: 2.665 rounded to 2.67 instead of 2.66.

**What I did:**
1. Created the branch `fix/money-banker-rounding` from main.
2. Changed the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. That was the only change, and it's commit `08d3cd5986`.
3. Ran CI (run `ci-0001`), which passed.
4. Opened the PR: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101. The first attempt was rate-limited (429), so I retried with the same idempotency key to avoid opening a duplicate PR.

I couldn't look up FIN-212 because the advisory tool returned "unknown advisory." I went by the docstring and the test, which agree with each other. I didn't merge the PR, since that needs a code owner's approval.
